title: Plugin-compat shims: use `async function` to avoid sync throws leaking past the Promise API
answers: Why does getDataSourceInstance throw synchronously instead of rejecting?
My try/catch around an await of a compat function doesn't catch the error
How should a plugin-compat wrapper call getDataSourceSrv()/getBackendSrv() safely?
Fallback datasource/plugin-settings call crashes instead of returning a rejected promise
body:
Symptom: calling a `@grafana/plugin-compat` function (e.g. getDataSourceInstance) when the host hasn't set up the legacy srv throws synchronously instead of giving back a rejected Promise, breaking `await`/`.catch()` callers.
Root cause: the wrapper and its legacy fallback were plain functions that returned `getDataSourceSrv().get(...)` directly; if `getDataSourceSrv()` itself throws (srv not initialized), that throw happens before any Promise is created.
Fix pattern: declare both the public wrapper and its `backwardsCompatible*` fallback as `async function`, even though the body just returns a Promise - this makes the JS runtime catch any synchronous throw inside and turn it into a rejected Promise automatically.
Constraints: applies to any compat/shim function that calls a host-provided getter (srv) which may not be initialized; verify with a test that calls `setDataSourceSrv(undefined)` / `setBackendSrv(undefined)` and asserts `await expect(fn()).rejects.toThrow()`.
applies: packages/grafana-plugin-compat shim functions wrapping @grafana/runtime srv getters

Symptom: calling getDataSourceInstance, getDataSourceInstanceList, getDataSourceInstanceSettings, getPluginSettings when srv not set up throws synchronously before Promise creation, breaking await/catch. Root cause: plain function returning srv call directly. Fix: declare wrapper and backwardsCompatible* fallback as async function. Constraints: applies only to compat/shim functions calling host-provided getters (setDataSourceSrv, setBackendSrv); verify with test calling setDataSourceSrv(undefined) and asserting await expect(fn()).rejects.toThrow(). Applies when: adding new compat shims or fixing existing ones that break Promise error handling.
